subject: gk
question: In India, there are various crops produced. Which group of crops belong to the pulses?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gram and tur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Gram (chickpea)** and **tur (pigeon pea)** are two of the most commonly grown pulse crops in India.

• These pulses are a major source of protein in the Indian diet, especially for vegetarians.

• Pulses like gram and tur play a crucial role in crop rotation and soil health improvement due to their nitrogen-fixing ability.

• India is one of the largest producers and consumers of pulses in the world, contributing significantly to the global pulse market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Other Common Pulses in India:**

• Other important pulses grown in India include lentils (masoor), mung beans, urad beans, and peas.

• These pulses are cultivated across various states, each having its specific climatic and soil preferences.

• **Nutritional Value:**

• Pulses are rich in proteins, dietary fiber, vitamins, and essential minerals like iron, magnesium, and potassium.

• They are considered vital for nutritional security, especially in regions with high rates of malnutrition.

• **Agricultural Practices:**

• Pulses are often grown in rotation with cereal crops to enhance soil fertility and reduce pest and disease cycles.

• They require less water compared to other crops and can thrive in semi-arid conditions, making them suitable for diverse agro-climatic zones.

• **Economic Importance:**

• The cultivation of pulses provides livelihood to millions of farmers across India.

• Pulses have significant export potential, contributing to the country's economy.
